title: Button
overview: A control that commits an action on this screen.
apply_when: The press does something here: save, submit, delete, open a dialog, go to the next step, or show in-flight state on the control.
not_when: The press only takes them to another page (link), or flips a setting that should persist as a toggle. Field labels stay design_a_form.

vs.why: navigation to another page or section
binary on/off that should persist as state

role.overview: The one action this view is for.
role.apply_when: One commit: Submit, Save, Continue, Start, Next.
role.not_when: A second equally loud action on the same view.

role.overview: A real action, quieter than the commit.
role.apply_when: Cancel, Back, Reset next to a primary.
role.not_when: This is the only action — then it is primary.

role.overview: Lowest emphasis; do not compete with the commit.
role.apply_when: A third option, a card action, a toast action, or ghost/text.
role.not_when: The page's main task — that is primary.

role.overview: The action removes or cannot be undone.
role.apply_when: Delete, Remove, Clear all, GOV.UK warning, Ant danger.
role.not_when: An ordinary commit dressed as danger for emphasis.

size.overview: Highest in the size hierarchy — the easiest to hit.
size.apply_when: The view's main commit, full-width on a small viewport, USWDS big.
size.not_when: A dense toolbar or a third option next to the commit.

size.apply_when: Ordinary actions in forms, dialogs, and page chrome.
size.not_when: The only action on a mobile screen that should span the width.

size.overview: Lowest in the size hierarchy — densest.
size.apply_when: Inline or toolbar actions that sit beside content.
size.not_when: The page's primary commit, or a control under 44×44.

composition.overview: Label only — the action is the words.
composition.apply_when: The verb is enough: Save, Cancel, Delete, Continue, Next.
composition.not_when: The control has no visible text and no accessible name.

composition.overview: Icon plus label — icon clarifies, label names.
composition.apply_when: A known action that still needs a verb.

composition.overview: Icon only — the name is not on screen.
composition.apply_when: A repeated, known control in chrome (close, settings).
composition.not_when: A one-off or destructive action with no accessible name.

composition.overview: Primary press plus a second control for more options.
composition.apply_when: One default action and a short related list.
composition.not_when: The menu repeats the primary phrase.

state.overview: At rest, available, not being used.
state.not_when: Work is in flight, or the control is not available.

state.overview: Pointer is over the control — extra cue, not the only cue.
state.apply_when: A mouse or trackpad can reach the control.
state.not_when: Hover is the only way to know it is a button (fails on touch).

state.overview: Keyboard or assistive tech is on this control. Must stay visible.
state.apply_when: Tab, Enter, Space, or restoring focus after a dialog.
state.not_when: Focus outline removed with no replacement; or autofocus on destructive.
A sticky pressed look after the action has finished.

state.overview: The action is not available. Must stay perceivable and explain why.
state.apply_when: Settings Save with a visible reason; or a control that must not run.
state.not_when: Public question submit — keep it enabled and explain on press. Dual-cite govuk.dont-use-disabled-buttons and fluent disabled-field perceivable.

state.overview: The action started; a second press must not send again.
state.apply_when: A request is in flight (save, submit, upload). Card compose_feedback when the spinner is on the control; cite forms.submit.enabled_until_request / govuk.stop-accidental-double-submit.
state.not_when: A spinner with no name, or the icon-only control replaced by a spinner.

accessibility.overview: The control has a name assistive tech can speak.
accessibility.apply_when: Any button, especially icon-only or a label that is an icon.
accessibility.not_when: The only name is a tooltip that never reaches the button.

accessibility.overview: The focused control stays visible. Color alone is not the cue.
accessibility.apply_when: Keyboard or AT focus is on the button.

accessibility.overview: Unavailable stays in the tab order and explains why.
accessibility.apply_when: The action must not run, but focus must not jump away.
accessibility.not_when: The HTML disabled attribute, which drops the control from the keyboard flow.

accessibility.overview: In-flight work is announced; the name and icon stay.
accessibility.apply_when: Save, submit, or upload has started.
accessibility.not_when: A spinner that replaces the icon-only control with no live name.

accessibility.overview: A button that stays down exposes pressed state.
accessibility.apply_when: Pin, follow, or another sticky on/off on a button.
accessibility.not_when: A setting that should be a toggle, not a button.

accessibility.overview: A button that opens something exposes open/closed.
accessibility.apply_when: The press reveals a menu, panel, or more content.
accessibility.not_when: A plain commit that does not reveal UI.

accessibility.overview: The hit area stays usable, including at small size.
accessibility.apply_when: Touch, pointer, or a compact toolbar button.
accessibility.not_when: A 24px icon whose tap area is the glyph only.

keyboard.overview: Tab lands on the button in a logical order.
keyboard.apply_when: Moving through the page or a dialog.
keyboard.not_when: The control is skipped because it used HTML disabled.

keyboard.overview: Enter runs the same action as a click.
keyboard.apply_when: The button is focused and the person confirms.
keyboard.not_when: Enter only works on submit, not on type=button.

keyboard.overview: Space runs the same action as a click.
keyboard.not_when: Space scrolls the page instead of activating.

keyboard.overview: After the action closes a surface, focus returns to the trigger.
keyboard.apply_when: The button opened a modal, menu, or popover that just closed.
keyboard.not_when: Focus dumped on the document body.
